articles.title: Concerns about the growth of AI companies are lowering the stock market
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
After positive tones on the European stock exchanges yesterday, stock markets in the US declined, a development that gained further momentum during Asian trading this morning. As usual, technology companies are in the main focus. Ahead of the reporting season, worrying questions are now being asked whether the large AI investments can be backed up by growth. This is especially true now as investments are not only made on borrowed money, but also coincide with the recent sharp rise in interest rates. The decline in Japan is 2.5% while the South Korean KOSPI is down almost 7%. Stock market futures ahead of the opening in Europe and the US clearly point to negative numbers. Oil prices are falling slightly after three days of gains and are now trading around USD 105 per barrel, for more on the current situation see Bjarne's comment 
here
. 
Yesterday, German Chancellor Merz said that the government will reduce the tax on electricity to the EU's minimum level (from the current 2% to the equivalent of 0.05%). He pointed out that it is just as important to support households, as it is to make new long-term reforms.
Today's statistical calendar can be described as averagely interesting.
 The focus is on the details of German inflation statistics if they give a different picture than the overall figures published earlier. From the US, we are of course looking at the small business barometer, ADP employment and home sales. 
New IMF forecast
 under the heading "Resilience under pressure, urgent elections". The IMF has increased global growth by a tenth for this year. The message is that AI investments counteract the negative repercussions of high energy prices. Reduced inventory levels have also counteracted the lower supply of oil. The IMF also notes that the margins of the measures that have affected resilience are not unlimited, and points out that the risk picture is on the downside. The rapidly rising interest rates mean that the IMF urges that it is urgent to do something about the budget deficits. For more, much more, read 
here
.
A hint for the Fed governor?
 This year's economics laureates, Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, have clarified the role of forward-looking expectations in how stabilization policy affects businesses and households, and are thus extremely close to the work we do. But the fact that they are receiving the award now, just as the new Fed Chair Warsh wants to make the Fed less transparent, is perhaps not a pure coincidence  
Nordic key stories
From an ecnomic point of view, it's a bit of an in-between day ahead of tomorrow's KPI details. But to get an overall picture of the Swedish market situation, Sweden360 "Swedish safe haven" is recommended, 
here
.
Today, Magdalena Andersson, Social Democrats and Speaker Norlén are meeting
 to 
 review the situation after the latest round of exploratory talks. Regardless of the conditions, this means that a first vote on the prime minister can take place on Thursday.
The price of petrol in Sweden has now found its way up a bit above SEK 19 per liter and is approaching the peak level in April. In Finland, you pay almost SEK 27 and in Denmark SEK 30. Electricity prices remain high in bidding area 4, which has again pulled away from the other areas, and the daily price is SEK 1.70/KWh.

articles.title: Oro för AI-bolagens tillväxt sänker börsen
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Efter positiva tongångar på Europabörserna igår backade börserna i USA, en utveckling som fått ytterligare kraft under den asiatiska handeln nu på morgonen. Teknikbolagen står som vanligt i huvudfokus. Inför rapportsäsongen ställs nu oroväckande frågor huruvida de stora AI-investeringarna kan backas upp av tillväxt. Det gäller framför allt nu när investeringarna inte bara görs på lånade pengar utan också sammanfaller med den senaste tidens kraftiga ränteuppgång. Nedgången i Japan ligger på 2,5% medan Sydkoreanska KOSPI är ned nästan 7%. Börsterminer inför öppningen i Europa och USA pekar tydligt på negativa siffror. Oljepriset backar något efter tre dagars uppgång och handlas nu omkring 105 USD per fat, för mer om nuläget se Bjarnes kommentar 
här
. 
Igår sa Tysklands förbundskansler Merz att regeringen ska sänka skatten på el till EU:s miniminivå (från dagens 2% till motsvarande 0.05%). Han poängterade att det är lika viktigt att stötta hushåll, som att göra nya långsiktiga reformer.
Dagens statistikkalender kan väl betecknas som genomsnittligt intressant.
 Fokus ligger på detaljerna i tysk inflationsstatistik om de ger en annan bild än de övergripande siffrorna som publicerats tidigare. Från USA tittar vi så klart på småföretagarbarometern, ADP-sysselsättningen och bostadsförsäljningar. 
Ny IMF-prognos
 under rubriken ”Motståndskraft under press, brådskande val”. IMF har skruvat upp världstillväxten en tiondel för i år. Budskapet är att AI-investeringar motverkar negativa efterverkningar från höga energipriser. Neddragna lagernivåer har också motverkat det lägre utbudet av olja. IMF noterar också att marginalerna av de åtgärder som påverkat motståndskraften inte är obegränsade, och poängterar att riskbilden ligger på nedsidan. De snabbt stigande räntorna gör att IMF uppmanar att det är bråttom att göra något åt budgetunderskotten. För mer, mycket mer, läs 
här
.
Passning till Fed-chefen?
 Årets ekonomipristagare, Robert E. Hall och Michael Woodford, har tydliggjort framåtblickande förväntningars roll för hur stabiliseringspolitiken påverkar företag och hushåll, och ligger därmed ytterst nära det arbete vi gör. Men att de nu får priset när den nya Fed-chefen Warsh vill göra Fed mindre transparent är kanske inte ett rent sammanträffande.
Sverige
Ekonomiskt är det lite av en 
mellandag
 inför morgondagens KPI-detaljer. Men för att få en övergripande bild kring svenskt marknadsläge rekommenderas Sweden360 ”Swedish safe haven”, 
här
.
Idag träffas Magdalena Andersson och talman Norlén
 för att gå igenom läget efter den senaste sonderingsrundan. Oaktat förutsättningar, så innebär det att en första statsministeromröstning kan ske på torsdag.
Bensinpriset har nu letat sig upp en bit över 19 kronor/liter och snuddar toppnivån i april. I Finland betalar man närmare 27 kronor och i Danmark 30 kronor. Elpriserna är fortsatt höga i elområde 4, som återigen dragit ifrån de andra områdena, och dagsnoteringen ligger på 1,70 kr/KWh.

articles.title: India’s Central Bank Plays For Time
articles.heading: Asia Alert
articles.fulltext:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is once again defending its USD/INR line in the sand at 97. Plunging reserves and heavy forward liabilities leave RBI little room to maneuver. Its weekend package builds friction to stem losses without draining reserves. Though not its first creative rescue, earlier policy reversals keep investors wary. Regulatory creativity can buy time. We keep our year-end USD/INR target at 96, trusting tinkering holds the dam until cheaper crude returns.
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) stepped up its rupee defense with a fresh package of measures. 
When the central bank delivered its first 25 bps hike in nearly four years on 7th October, the promise of “calibrated” tightening did not impress traders. The market promptly sold the rupee past 96.8 against the greenback, prompting the central bank to once again defend its line in the sand at 97 per dollar (Chart 1). 
Chart 1: RBI is still defending rupee at 97 per dollar level
Source: Bloomberg, SEB
India’s FX reserves have been on wild ride this year, reflecting RBI’s efforts to prop up its currency. 
After peaking at USD 711 billion in January 2026, the war in Iran and subsequent spike in oil prices prompted the RBI to burn through USD 37 billion in March to prop up the rupee. The FCNR(B) deposit scheme fueled a summer recovery, pushing reserves to a new record of USD 785.7 billion by early September. Yet, shuttering the program just as crude oil prices surged again wiped out USD 51 billion in a month (Chart 2). The RBI’s net dollar forward book further magnifies the extent of currency intervention. The net short dollar forward position has expanded substantially, reaching a record USD 136.8 billion by July. 
The large contingent liability leaves the RBI with far less room to maneuver in the future.
 Chart 2: FX reserves have been on a wild ride with forward positions magnifying the FX intervention
Source: Bloomberg, SEB
Thus, the RBI rolled out yet another patchwork defense for the rupee over the weekend 10-11 October.
 In the hope to spare its yet again declining reserves, state-run oil companies were shunted to a special dollar window, off the spot market. To stifle speculative activity, the central bank borrowed a trick from Beijing with the introduction of the Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve for FX derivatives. Lenders are now required to set aside 20% reserves of the notional value of each derivative transaction above USD 2 million. Meanwhile, the RBI is also prohibiting the immediate rebooking of cancelled FX contracts. The RBI has also aggressively slashed limits for derivatives trading without underlying exposure to USD 5 million from USD 100 million. Overall, 
the new package has built a wall of friction against further rupee weakness while limiting the decline in FX reserves.
This is not the first time the RBI got creative in its support of the rupee with a package of measures to attract foreign currency in June. 
As foreign reserves had been declining since March, the RBI launched a special swap window that encouraged banks to offer 3-5 year foreign currency deposits. The hedging costs of the foreign currency non-resident FCNR(B) deposits program were absorbed by the central bank, lowering the overall cost of funds for banks. Tax breaks were also introduced for foreign bond investors. Market access for foreign investors in bonds and equities was likewise eased. The package hauled in USD 56.85 billion, with FCNR(B) deposits accounting for more than USD 52 billion. This allowed the RBI to rebuild its official reserves. Yet, faced with an estimate USD 9-12 billion bill over five years if deposits continued to soar, the central bank unexpectedly pulled the plug by end-August. 
The decision to close the program early gave investors a fresh dose of policy confusion and the impression that policymakers are sensitive to the price tag. 
The RBI can still pull more levers to keep the rupee from falling past 97 in the near term. 
The initial bounce towards 95.6 looks fleeting. The rise in NDF points reveals that 3-month market expectations remain firmly above 97. RBI’s latest wall of friction buys time, but it cures no ills. High oil prices, robust dollar and declining capital flows will resume sapping the rupee’s recovery. 
For now, we keep our yearend USD/INR forecast at 96, trusting that the regulatory creativity can keep the dam intact until cheaper crude oil returns.

articles.title: The Trump diesel charade
articles.heading: Crude oil comment
articles.fulltext:
Brent higher last week and today as fresh attacks by Iran and the Houthis shattered a sense of temporary normality exports from the Persian Gulf.
 Brent crude traded in a range of $97.06 - 105.92/b and closed the week at $104.72/b. The Brent Dec contract gained $2.47/b on the week. Fresh attacks by Iran on ships in the Gulf and the SoH probably reduced exports of oil through the SoH last week. Exports from the Persian Gulf had reached close to normal levels in the second half of September and into early October. This has led to a large increase in oil on water globally which has helped to ease and reduce November and December prices over the past month. The sense of some kind of normality of exports from the SoH was shattered last week. Fresh attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia added to this and helped to lift prices. It is well known that the US and its allies in the Gulf are running low on defensive rockets. Hard choices over what to defend will increasingly have to be made: Oil infrastructure, military installations, royal palaces, civilian airports or other. The US will also have to decide how many defensive rockets it can provide to its ME allies versus what it needs for its own defenses. Ukraine is at least not getting any of these defensive rockets however much needed for defense against a continuous barrage of Russian attacks on Ukraine. The front-month ICE Gasoil 10ppm (essentially ULSFO Diesel) is down 3.8% this morning (due to Trump's diesel charade) to $1427/ton ($191/b) which is where it traded last Thursday.
Trump's diesel charade. 
The site "535" now puts the probability for control of the US Congress and Senate following the midterm elections at 99% and 61% respectively. Trump's war in the Middle East with high or record high gasoline and diesel prices at the pump in the US is largely to blame. Trump's diesel deal with Russia is clearly Trump trying to shift the blame from his own war in the ME to Ukraine instead. He could of course have placed the blame on Putin and Russia for its war against Ukraine, but no, it is Ukraine who gets the blame and not the least Zelenskyy. Physically it is of course correct that it is Ukraine who is destroying Russian refineries to the point where 45% of Russian refineries are out of operation. The result is that there is too little gasoline for domestic Russian consumption and no diesel, VGO and Jet fuel left over for exports. Russia normally (pre-war 2022) exports some 1.3-1.4 mb/d of diesel products of which a lot used to go to Europe.
Russia/Putin would happily export diesel products to the world, but it can't
 because Ukraine is destroying its refineries. Russia implemented export restrictions of diesel already in July this year and the plan was to extend that to early 2027.
The only way that Putin/Russia can start sustained diesel exports, is if Trump is able to discipline and prevent Ukraine from attacking and destroying Russian refineries.
 Then Russian refineries can be repaired, ramp up, produce more diesel and potentially export what ever is of surplus to the world. Trump has threatened Ukraine that if it doesn't stop its attacks on Russian refineries, then there will be no more indirect sales of weapons from the US via Europe to Ukraine and the intelligence which US currently is providing to Ukraine will stop.
It is clear that if Russia stops its attacks on Ukraine, then Ukraine is prepared for a energy infrastructure cease-fire.
Trump very well knows that he has himself to blame
 for the terrible stats for the upcoming midterm elections where Republicans looks set to lose both the Senate and the House. This is a charade for the US public to shift the blame over to something or someone else than himself. His easy choice falls on Ukraine and Zelenskyy for which he has shown little love, affection and support. Nothing of the one way bromance which Trump has shown versus Putin.
At most a three-week holdup in Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. Ukraine accepting to play scapegoat.
 Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries and oil infrastructure is a key element of Ukraine fighting back and defending itself against Russia. Ukraine has no choice but to continue its attacks as long as Russia keeps attacking Ukraine. But maybe there can be a three week holdup where Ukraine is forced by the US to step down its attacks on Russian refineries to please Trump until the US midterm elections are behind us. I.e. Ukraine accepting to be the scapegoat for Trump's missteps in the Middle East for a three week period. Thereafter it will revert back to well thought out strategy of attacking Russian oil and refinery installations.  
Trump under increasing pressure as there is increasing probability for Democratic victory in US midterm elections. Desperate times and desperate measures from Trump as a result. More to come
Source: 535 — 2026 midterms forecast, https://535.wtf/
Large increase in oil on water heading for consumers around the world following a sharp increase in exports of oil from the Persian Gulf to close to normal from mid-Sep. Lower exports last week after new hostilities most likely. 
Source: SEB graph and highlights, Bloomberg data feed from Vortexa

articles.title: Swedish safe haven
articles.heading: Sweden 360
articles.fulltext:
Sweden 360 provides you with a quick and broad overview of Swedish macro, rates and FX.
*** See attachment for full report ***
Macro highlights: Back-to-back Riksbank hikes look unlikely
CPIF ex energy came in at 0.53% y/y, 0.16pp below SEB and 0.21pp below the Riksbank. 
Adjusted for VAT cuts and subsidies, core inflation was unchanged at 1.5% y/y, with
annualised monthly momentum at just 1.1%. 
Services and food drove the downside 
surprise
. 
C
ore 
goods inflation rose, 
driven
by SEK depreciation and higher electronics prices.
September reinforces our view that summer inflation was partly temporary. We expect a gradual rise in core inflation over the next 6-12 months, but near-term momentum remains subdued. 
Headline inflation set to rise on energy, mainly due to the reversal of temporary fuel tax cuts in Q4. Electricity prices are also set to rise during the winter.
Against this backdrop, 
back-to-back rate hikes from the Riksbank looks unlikely
. We see a November hike as highly probable but expect a second hike won’t arrive until 2027. We reiterate 
our view 
that 
the market is pricing too much in total from the Riksbank given the high interest rate sensitivity of the Swedish economy.
Rates highlights: SGBs look marginally expensive
FX highlights: Market narrative turns SEK into ‘safe haven light’ vs EUR
French bond risk fears set of a near-term correction in SEK as EUR broke lower. 
We are sticking with our view that this is 
a phase of tactical position reduction in SEK (covering shorts). 
Aggregated positioning still very short in SEK (vs EUR, USD & NOK), similar to fellow low-yielder CHF (vs EUR, USD).
CHF the better option of the two if equities start correcting. Current environment is one of risk-off in FI spreads but with equities the odd one out, should equities correct CHF will do better than SEK. More on recent views 
here
.
Fundamentally – from a regime perspective, not much has changed. SEK needs a bigger global disinflation impulse and lower global yields to see real turnaround –this is more likely to be a story of 2027.
Upcoming data and events
Labour market indicators have improved slightly but do not support a sharp acceleration for employment.
 The labour force survey (LFS) continues to be very volatile with both high unemployment and high employment during the summer. We predict both exployment and unemployment to decline in September. Alternative measures imply gradually rising employment.
Retail sales and household consumption have been very strong during the summer, but we predict household consumption to fall back slightly in September. 
Consumer confidence has finally improved more markedly and momentum for consumption is currently strong. However, we predict headwinds from sharply higher energy prices and early rate hikes from the Riksbank, and risks to our optimistic forecast for 2027 have shifted to the downside.
Week Ahead:

articles.title: Desperate, vote-chasing Trump buys Putin’s diesel
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Impressive equity market resilience despite the interest rate headache – conclusions.
 We are on the verge of an unusually interesting earnings season, with expectations of solid results for Q3 2026. The economic outlook is getting a tailwind (more below), despite serious wars, confusing politics and a dramatic upward shift in the entire yield curve – driven by both cyclical and structural forces. US equities closed near record highs on Friday: S&P 500 +0.6% and Nasdaq +0.5%. Stockholm’s OMXSPI gained 1.6%. 
President Trump’s tragic decision to temporarily lift US sanctions on Russian diesel producers
 (more below) changes the playing field for Ukraine. Brent crude closed at an elevated USD 105 per barrel on Friday (current level 103 dollar); 
the Houthis’ deadly attacks on Riyadh airport
 confirm the continued serious security situation in the region. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.25% (+2 basis points). Meanwhile, Paris is forced to confront the embarrassing fact that 
France’s serious fiscal problems
 mean it now pays a record 30 basis points more than Italy to borrow for 10 years: 4.85% versus 4.55%. What raises alarm bells for economists is France’s weak, “almost dead”, productivity growth (see charts). This sets the stage for unsustainable debt dynamics in the longer term. Today is 
Columbus Day in the US
; the bond market is closed, while equity markets remain open. 
Asian stock markets are trading cautiously in early Monday trading, with a slightly positive bias; Japan’s markets are closed for a holiday. U.S. and European stock futures are up 0.3–0.6%.
“Prices will fall rapidly and by record amounts” – reflections.
 Donald Trump predicts lower diesel prices after reaching an agreement with Putin on sanctions relief. The White House is lifting sanctions on Russian diesel producers until April next year. A desperate and short-sighted Trump, known for his many U-turns, is chasing votes ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. 
The backlash has been strong
. The decision ties Ukraine’s hands when it comes to attacking Russian energy infrastructure. 
Meanwhile, Trump says
: “It’s time for Ukraine to get a new president.” 
Ukraine’s Zelenskyy calls it terrible news: “This looks like an outright birthday present for Putin.”
EU and China avoid a trade war (at least for now) – some thoughts.
 The EU has a destabilising imbalance in goods trade with China, with a deficit of no less than EUR 360bn in 2025. 
China has now agreed
, among other things, to cut its exports of hybrid cars to the EU by more than half over a four-year period. Beijing is also promising a so-called green channel to facilitate exports of rare earth elements to the EU. The agreement covers 
16 specific areas where the two sides have reached common ground
. The next high-level meeting will take place in March 2027. China clearly remains attracted by access to the EU’s 450 million potential consumers.
IMF expected to confirm resilient growth, but with downside risks – conclusions.
 When the IMF releases its new forecasts tomorrow, the outlook is relatively bright, despite repeated shocks since the pandemic in 2020. Three issues are in focus: (1) the impact of rapid advances in 
AI technology and its capacity for self-improvement
, (2) 
the return of inflation risks
 and (3) 
record-high public debt
.
"No" to an expanding EU budget.
 Ireland’s new, scaled-back 
proposal for the EU’s 2028–2034 budget
 faces strong opposition. “The EU needs a better budget, not a bigger one,” says Sweden’s Minister for EU Affairs, Rosencrantz.
Nordic key stories
Patience is needed even as time is running out – some reflections.
 Tomorrow, the Swedish Social Democratic Party leader will report to the Speaker of Parliament on the government formation talks. Friday’s meeting between the red-green party leaders can be summed up in three words: necessary, constructive, inconclusive. Expectations of a breakthrough were low, but the participants seemed satisfied. The red lines remain as clear as ever. Patience is needed, but Speaker Norlén is likely to step up the pressure on all eight parliamentary parties to give and take. Markets have continued to keep the government formation process off their radar, probably for good reason. After all, the government formation debacle in autumn 2018 barely left a mark on financial markets.
Sweden should do this too.
 China is planning a new employment initiative to align workforce skills with advances in AI. It includes support for university graduates and other young people, as well as better working conditions for people in flexible and emerging forms of employment in the wake of AI. 
Epilogue:
 Sweden’s future labour market needs a well-functioning and effective transition system that provides both financial security and opportunities for continuous skills development as jobs come and go.
Good publicity for Sweden and Saab:
“Thailand's queen becomes first female royal to fly fighter jet.”

articles.title: Desperat och röstfiskande Trump köper Putin-diesel
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Imponerande börsstyrka trots räntehuvudvärk – slutsatser
. Vi står på tröskeln till en ovanligt spännande rapportsäsong, med förväntningar på solida resultat för tredje kvartalet 2026. Konjunkturen ger medvind (mer nedan) trots allvarliga krig, förvirrande politik och ett dramatiskt lyft av hela avkastningskurvan – både konjunkturellt och strukturellt drivet. USA-börserna stängde i fredags nära rekordnivåer: S&P 500 +0,6% och Nasdaq +0,5%. Stockholms OMXSPI lyfte 1,6%. 
President Trumps tragiska beslut att tillfälligt häva USA-sanktioner mot ryska dieselproducenter
 (mer nedan) ändrar spelplanen för Ukraina. Brentoljan stängde i fredags på höga 105 dollar per fat (handlas i dag till 103 dollar); 
huthiernas dödliga attacker mot Riyadhs flygplats
 bekräftar det fortsatt allvarliga säkerhetspolitiska läget i regionen. USA 10-årsränta stängde på 5,25% (+2 räntepunkter). I Paris tvingas man samtidigt dra den pinsamma slutsatsen att 
Frankrikes allvarliga statsfinansiella läge
 gör att man idag betalar rekordhöga 0,3%-enheter mer än Italien för att låna 10-åriga pengar; 4,85% mot 4,55%. Det som får ekonomen att hissa varningsflagg är Frankrikes svaga, ”nästintill döda”, produktivitet (se bilder). Det bäddar för en långsiktigt ohållbar skulddynamik. Idag firas 
Columbus Day
 i bl a USA; räntemarknaden håller stängt men börserna är öppna. 
Börserna i Asien tidig måndag handlas avvaktande, med en försiktigt positiv underton; Japan håller marknadsstängt. USA:s och Europas börsterminer stiger 0,3–0,6%. 
”Priserna kommer falla snabbt och rekordmycket” – reflektioner
.
Donald Trump spår lägre priser på diesel efter att ha slutit avtal med Putin om sanktionslättnader. Vita huset lyfter sanktionerna mot ryska dieselproducenter fram till april nästa år. En desperat
och
kortsiktig
Trump,
känd för sina många U-svängar, jagar röster inför mellanårsvalet den 3 november. 
Reaktionerna är starka
. Beslutet bakbinder Ukrainas möjligheter att attackera rysk energiinfrastruktur. 
Samtidigt säger Trump
: ”Det är dags för Ukraina att få en ny president”. 
Ukrainas Zelenskyj säger att det är ett fruktansvärt besked: ”Det här ser ut som rena födelsedagspresenten till Putin”
. 
EU–Kina undviker 
(i alla fall just nu) 
handelskrig – tankar.
 EU har en destabiliserande obalans i varuhandeln med Kina, med ett underskott på hela 360 miljarder euro 2025. 
Nu har Kina gått med på
 att under fyra år bl a begränsa exporten av hybridbilar till EU med mer än hälften. Peking utlovar även en s k grön kanal som ska underlätta exporten av sällsynta jordartsmetaller till EU. Överenskommelsen omfattar 
16 specifika områden där parterna nått samsyn
. Nästa högnivåmöte hålls i mars 2027. Det är uppenbart att Kina fortsatt lockas av tillgången till EU 450 miljoner potentiella konsumenter.
IMF väntas bekräfta motståndskraftig tillväxt med bakslagsrisker – slutsatser
. När IMF presenterar nya prognoser i morgon är bilden förhållandevis ljus, trots återkommande chocker sedan pandemin 2020. Tre frågor står i fokus: (1) effekterna av den snabba utvecklingen av 
AI-tekniken och dess förmåga till självförbättring
, (2) 
inflationsriskernas återkomst
 och (3) 
rekordhöga offentliga skulder
.
Nej till svällande EU-budget
. Det irländska nya nedbantade 
förslaget till EU-budget för 2028-2034
 möter starkt motstånd: ”EU behöver en bättre budget, inte en större”, säger Sveriges EU-minister Rosencrantz.
Sverige
Tålamod krävs trots att sanden sinar i timglaset – reflektioner.
 I morgon ska Socialdemokraternas partiledare rapportera till talmannen om regeringssonderingarna. Fredagens möte mellan de rödgröna partiledarna kan sammanfattas med tre ord: nödvändigt, konstruktivt, regeringsfattigt. Förväntningarna på genombrott var låga, men deltagarna verkade nöjda. De röda linjerna kvarstår, lika tydliga som tidigare. Tålamod krävs, men talmannen Norlén lär öka pressen på samtliga åtta riksdagspartier att både ge och ta. Marknaden har fortsatt regeringsfrågan utanför radarn, sannolikt av goda skäl. Regeringsdebaclet hösten 2018 lämnade ju knappt några avtryck på de finansiella marknaderna.
Det här borde Sverige också göra.
 Kina planerar ett nytt sysselsättningsinitiativ för att anpassa arbetskraftens kompetens till AI-utvecklingen. Det omfattar stöd till universitetsutbildade och andra unga samt bättre arbetsvillkor för personer med flexibla och nya anställningsformer i kölvattnet på AI. 
Epilog:
 Framtidens svenska arbetsmarknad behöver ett väl fungerande och effektivt omställningssystem som ger såväl ekonomisk trygghet som möjlighet till kontinuerlig kompetensutveckling när jobben kommer och går.
Bra reklam för Sverige och Saab
: 
”Thailands drottning första kvinnliga monarken som flyger stridsflyg.”

articles.title: Inflation, IMF and Global Meetings in Focus
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
US CPI and PPI figures will be next week’s data highlight, together with Swedish final CPI. US activity data will also be watched ahead of the Fed’s policy rate decision on 28 October. The IMF will publish its three flagship reports during the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok. The G20 Finance Ministers meeting and the European Council meeting on 15–16 October add to the international policy agenda. In the euro area, revised inflation figures and several ECB speeches will also be in focus, while Norway’s data calendar remains thin.  
US:
September CPI and PPI data will be the final key releases ahead of the Fed’s policy rate decision on 28 October. Activity data – retail sales and industrial production – will be watched for judging the economic momentum going into the Fed decision. The Fed will release its Beige Book, and we will get the first regional surveys for October. The coming week will be the last chance for Fed members to convey their views before the Fed enters its silent period next weekend. Fed Chair Warsh will appear in a fire-side chat with the IMF’s Georgieva on Friday.
Euro area: 
No major data releases. We will get revised inflation figures for September. We will also keep an eye on several ECB speeches and the EU summit on 15–16 October, where the next long-term EU budget and trade relations with China will be among the key topics on the agenda. 
Sweden:
Final September CPI is the most interesting metric this week. Money market inflation expectations, household consumption and the labour force survey will also be presented. The Riksbank’s Bunge speaks on Monday, the same day as Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson report on negotiations to form a new government to the speaker of parliament.
Norway:
Thin data calendar this week. Norges Bank’s Bank Lending Survey for Q3 will be published but is hardly a market mover.

articles.title: Re-acceleration in August
articles.heading: Swedish growth indicators
articles.fulltext:
Private sector production grew at a strong pace in August, re-accelerating after a slowdown in July.
 The monthly increase was 0.5%, in line with our forecast, but a revision to previous data lifted the year-on-year rate to 3.8%; somewhat higher than we had anticipated. Industrial production rebounded after a drop in July, bringing the year-on-year rate to a solid 5.8%. Monthly data are very volatile but the very positive underlying trend for the industry looks even stronger. New orders steadied following sharp swings in previous months, rising 5.5% y/y. Defence-related volatility in new orders is likely to continue ahead, as production and delivery of defense materials are often spread out over a number of years.
The GDP indicator came in at 1.1/3.5%
 - also in line with our forecast over the month but stronger on the yearly rate as previous numbers were revised higher. Most of the strong increases are reversals of weak readings in June and July and the average over July and August is largely unchanged compared to the average for Q2. The indicator thus signals weak quarterly growth in Q3, although this follows upon very strong growth in Q2. As we often point out, the monthly GDP indicator is highly volatile, often revised, and not necessarily a good indicator of actual growth. There are many signs of a broad-based, above-trend growth in Sweden, with sentiment indicators pointing to further strength ahead. Importantly, household consumption (September data published next week) is starting to increase more clearly. Some payback in Q3 is probable after the very strong Q2 (1.6%, 3.3% y/y), but both production and household consumption indicate upward risks to our Q3 forecast (0.2% q/q). 
We remain positive on the outlook for Swedish growth this year, seeing upside risks to our forecast that annual GDP will rise 2.7%.
 We forecast strong growth also in the coming year, but with households potentially hit by a cocktail of higher mortgage rates, higher energy prices and fading fiscal policy support, the growth outlook for 2027 might become considerably more subdued.

articles.title: CPI-ATE above Norges Bank’s forecast but slightly lower than expected
articles.heading: Norwegian inflation
articles.fulltext:
CPI-ATE was unchanged at 3.0%, slightly below our own and the consensus estimate but slightly above Norges Bank’s. Details were mixed with higher-than-expected food prices, but a relatively large decline for furniture prices worked in the opposite direction. We continue to see slightly higher core inflation than Norges Bank’s forecast in the next 3-6 months but predict slightly lower core inflation later in 2027.
Details: 
There were small differences for most items while there was a larger decline for other core goods, driven by furniture etc. Goods prices have been surprisingly high over the last 6-9 months, and this could be a bit of a payback. Stronger NOK should exert downward pressure on inflation over the next 12 months. Food prices declined less than normal. High food prices are a bit worrying, but food prices have been lower than expected since spring and volatility is high. Slightly lower service prices and rents are positive, but the deviations are small compared to monthly volatility.
Headline CPI increased to 3.4% from 3.3% y/y, which was 0.2-0.3pp lower than our forecast. As expected, fuel prices increased by almost 30% m/m, but electricity prices were unchanged and slightly below our forecast.
Implications Norges Bank:
 The downward revision to Norges Bank’s near-term trajectory (by 0.5pp) in its Sep26 MPR was surprisingly large. The 0.1ppt deviation in September (between consensus and Norges Bank’s estimate) should thus be rather neutral. However, we see a clear risk that the gap will widen in coming months. Though this will underpin current market pricing of a 50% chance for a Dec hike and a policy rate peak of 4.75%, we reiterate that we expect the policy rate peak to have been reached. Last year’s two rate cuts have now been reversed, and the Committee is clearly split on what’s deemed as a sufficiently restrictive policy. In the end, long-term inflation drivers will be decisive.

articles.title: Lower equities, lower oil prices, lower bond yields and lower AI revenues...
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The US stock markets fell yesterday, with the S&P 500 ending at -0.5% and the Nasdaq at -1.5%. It is usually either concerns about rising interest rates, higher oil prices or AI that make markets gloomy. Yesterday, it was mainly AI concerns that drove the decline after the FT reported that OpenAI's annual revenue would be significantly lower than previously communicated. Oil prices initially climbed yesterday but fell back after Trump said he will not carry out any attacks on Iran before the midterm elections. U.S. long-term interest rates also fell back after an auction of 30y bonds went well with strong demand. With the return on bonds now as high as the expected return on the stock market (graph 
here
), it is hardly surprising that investors are starting to turn back to fixed income investments again.
France vs. the market. 
 The large deficits in the French budget have caused the markets to trade up the interest rate spread against Germany to levels not seen since the euro crisis in 2011 (graph 
here
). However, my personal view is that it is difficult to be too worried and that a situation where the ECB would have to step in with support measures is a long way off. France is a rich country that is fully capable of solving its own problems. But unpopular austerity measures does not happen by itself. It requires the market to force French politicians to make uncomfortable but necessary decisions. Hopefully, this is the process we are seeing in France now, even if all forms of austerity lead to large protests. In this context, it can also be noted, with some satisfaction, that the worst-hit countries during the previous European debt crisis, the PIIGS countries, have all today got their public finances in order (graph 
here
). If they can, so can France. 
In Asia
 , the stock markets are mixed today, with Japan at -0.3% and Hong Kong at +1.1%. Ahead of the opening here at home, both European and American stock market futures are pointing upwards. There have only been small movements in the foreign exchange market. 
Swedish data focus. 
 We have a lot of interesting Swedish economic statistics on the agenda today. Industrial production and the order situation should come in reasonably well if the strong industrial sentiment we have had in August and September is to be believed. The GDP indicator, which fell in July, should also have turned around in August. In Norway, focus will be on new inflation numbers.
Nordic key stories
The Swedish economy is doing well. 
 Yesterday, outgoing Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson painted a bright picture of the Swedish economy, which she predicts will grow by 3% this year and a decent 2.7% in 2027. According to the Finance Minister, a broad upturn is expected that includes both households and companies. At the same time, the assessment from August remains that the scope for reform is only SEK 50 billion for the entire coming parliamentary term.
Have a great Friday.

articles.title: Lägre börser, lägre oljepris, lägre långräntor och lägre AI-intäkter…
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var deppigt på USA-börserna igår. S&P 500 slutade på -0,5% och Nasdaq backade hela 1,5%. Det brukar ju vara antingen oro för stigande räntor, högre oljepris eller AI som får marknaden att tappa sugen. Igår var det framför allt AI-oro som drev nedgången efter att FT rapporterat att OpenAI:s årliga intäkter skulle bli betydligt lägre än vad som tidigare har kommunicerats. Oljepriset klättrade inledningsvis under gårdagen men föll tillbaka efter att Trump sagt att han inte kommer att genomföra några attacker på Iran innan mellanårsvalet. Amerikanska långräntor föll också tillbaka efter att en auktion av 30-åringar gått bra med stark efterfrågan. Då avkastningen på obligationer nu är lika hög som den förväntade avkastningen på börsen (graf 
här
) är det knappast förvånande att investerare börjar vända tillbaka till ränteplaceringar igen.
Frankrike vs. marknaden. 
De stora underskotten i den franska budgeten har fått marknaderna att handla upp räntespreaden mot Tyskland till nivåer som vi inte sett sedan eurokrisen 2011 (graf 
här
). Min personliga åsikt är ändå att det är svårt att bli alltför oroad och att ett läge där ECB skulle behöva gå in med stödåtgärder är långt borta. Frankrike är i grunden ett rikt land som är fullt kapabelt att lösa sina egna problem. Men impopulära åtstramningar kommer inte av sig självt utan det krävs att marknaden drar åt tumskruvarna och tvingar franska politiker att fatta obekväma men nödvändiga beslut. Det är förhoppningsvis den processen vi ser i Frankrike nu, även om alla former av åtstramningar leder till stora protester. I det sammanhanget kan man också, med viss tillfredställelse, notera att de värst drabbade länderna under den förra europeiska skuldkrisen, PIIGS-länderna, samtliga idag har fått ordning på sina statsfinanser (graf 
här
). Kan de så kan Frankrike även om det tar emot. 
I Asien
 är det blandat på börserna idag med Japan på -0,3% och Hongkong på +1,1%. Inför öppningen här hemma pekar både europeiska och amerikanska börsterminer uppåt. Det har bara varit små rörelser på valutamarknaden. 
Svenskt datafokus. 
Vi har en hel del intressant svensk konjunkturstatistik på agendan idag. Industriproduktion och orderläge borde komma in hyfsat om man ska tro det starka industrisentimentet vi har haft i augusti och september. Även BNP-indikatorn som backade i juli bör ha svängt om i augusti. För de som är intresserade av vad som händer i vårt västra grannland Norge kommer där nya inflationssiffror.
Sverige
Svensk ekonomi går som tåget. 
Igår målade avgående finansminister Elisabeth Svantesson en ljus bild av svensk ekonomi som hon spår kommer att växa med 3% i år och hyfsade 2,7% 2027. Enligt finansministern väntar en bred uppgång som omfattar både hushåll och företag. Samtidigt kvarstår bedömningen från augusti om att reformutrymmet bara är 50 mdr för hela den kommande mandatperioden. 
Ha en bra (om än regnig) fredag.

articles.title: Can the EU persuade China to reduce exports?
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
US stock markets fell yesterday, albeit modestly and from high levels. The price of oil (Brent) has risen by a couple of dollars to USD 102 per barrel following new Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and concerns that the US is preparing new attacks on Iran. US yields rose yesterday, but the increase eased after a government bond auction attracted decent demand. Asian stock markets are in negative territory overnight, while futures point to modest declines in Europe and the US ahead of today’s trading. Apart from US labour market statistics, today’s economic data calendar is relatively light, but there are numerous central bank speakers from the ECB (plus accounts from September meeting), the Bank of England and the Fed, as well as the Riksbank’s Thedéen and Norges Bank’s Bache.
Fed minutes – the rate peak has not been reached, but a pause in October.
 The minutes from the September 15–16 meeting showed that all members supported the rate hike and that most saw a need for further tightening before year-end. Several factors underpinned the assessment: inflation – both actual developments and concerns about it – was naturally in focus, but growth and the labour market also played a role. Although the message is hawkish, it is fully in line with the signals in Fed members’ own rate projections, which were released in conjunction with the meeting, and is less hawkish than market pricing at the time of the meeting and thereafter. Financial conditions were seen as supportive, but some members wanted to be prepared for risks of market dysfunction. We expect the Fed to pause in October and deliver one further 25-basis-point hike in December. Read our comment 
here
.
Can the EU persuade China to reduce exports?
 Today and tomorrow, the EU and China are discussing trade and investment in Beijing. From the EU’s perspective, China’s large trade surplus is unsurprisingly a key focus. One area in which the EU hopes to make progress is limiting imports of Chinese hybrid cars, which have increased sharply recently, partly as a result of the EU raising import tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles. The fact that Germany and German carmakers are now pushing for import restrictions gives the EU greater weight on the issue, but China is reportedly opposed to such measures. Given China’s dependence on exports, the questions are how much it is prepared to concede, how far the EU can go unilaterally without provoking Chinese countermeasures, and whether a limited EU success would help or hinder the discussion on more extensive trade protection. The EU delegation will report back on the issue when the EU-leaders meet next week.
Recommended reading from us:
 An updated chart and analysis package on the war around the Persian Gulf (
here
), comments on the Norwegian government budget and fiscal policy (
here
), and industrial production (
here
).
Nordic key stories
Stronger trend in Swedish home prices.
 Data published by Svensk Mäklarstatistik this morning indicate a continued strong trend in the housing market. According to our own calculations, home prices have risen by almost 6% in total so far this year, or just over 3% on a seasonally adjusted basis. Revised data have removed some of the signs of weakness seen in recent months. A stronger trend is more consistent with our own home price indicator, the general improvement in consumer confidence, and the strong consumption data observed over the past six months.
Subdued underlying Swedish inflationary pressure despite high energy prices.
 Yesterday’s inflation figures were lower than expected for the second consecutive month. Energy prices are rising, but underlying inflationary pressure is more subdued. This supports our assessment that the higher inflation readings during the summer were partly temporary. This was the final inflation reading before the November rate decision. We expect the Riksbank to raise rates then, but the lower inflation readings may create some hesitation within the Executive Board. Read more 
here
.
